purpose: release_forge_publish_e2e_tests.rs and durable_release_e2e_tests.rs currently cover npm and PyPI publish paths only against fake providers, never a real registry server. This spec adds at least one e2e test per ecosystem (npm, PyPI) that publishes against a real local registry and confirms the published artifact is retrievable, while keeping existing fake-provider tests for fast iteration.
scope: crates/callisto-cli/tests/release_forge_publish_e2e_tests.rs and durable_release_e2e_tests.rs's npm and PyPI publish scenarios; CI installation of Verdaccio and pypiserver. Registry routing for these tests goes through each package manager's own configuration (npm --registry / .npmrc; twine --repository-url), not a callisto-side registry binding.
non_goals: A real local cargo registry e2e test -- cargo publish requires a registry index with an API that no lightweight local server provides; the existing hermetic file:// git-registry cargo test already covers observable publish behavior and is kept as-is.
Removing or changing the existing fake-provider tests in these files -- they remain for fast, hermetic iteration alongside the new real-registry tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An e2e test starts a local Verdaccio registry, points npm at it via --registry or a test-scoped .npmrc (not a callisto-side registry binding), runs callisto's npm publish path against it, and asserts the published version is retrievable from that registry's package metadata afterward. When the Verdaccio binary is not available in the environment, the test skips and prints the reason to test output rather than failing; the test is Linux-only (compiled out elsewhere), and CI installs Verdaccio on its Linux leg so the test runs there.

Given the Verdaccio registry in AC-20 is reachable only over http://127.0.0.1 (loopback), the test configures npm to accept that loopback origin via the package-manager's own config (--registry / .npmrc), not by relaxing callisto's UntrustedNpmRegistry/UnsafeRegistryBinding checks from SPEC-DX-CORRECTNESS-PARITY AC-4/AC-5.

An e2e test starts a local pypiserver instance, points twine at it via --repository-url (not a callisto-side registry binding), runs callisto's PyPI publish path against it, and asserts the published package/version is retrievable from that server's simple index afterward. When the pypiserver binary is not available, the test skips and prints the reason to test output rather than failing; the test is Linux-only (compiled out elsewhere), CI installs pypiserver on its Linux leg so the test runs there, and only loopback network access is required (no external network calls).

reasoning: Grounded against origin/fix/release-run-simplify@9be31095: release_forge_publish_e2e_tests.rs and durable_release_e2e_tests.rs confirmed to exist at crates/callisto-cli/tests/. Per GATE2-FIXES.md's SPEC-DX-RELEASE-CORRECTNESS decisions: AC-21 (real local cargo registry) is dropped because cargo publish needs a registry index with an API that no minimal local server provides cleanly, and the existing hermetic file:// git-registry test already covers observable behavior -- kept as a non-goal rather than silently omitted. AC-20/22 route registry access through each package manager's own config rather than a callisto binding, per the same notes, and AC-20b makes explicit that this routing must not require loosening callisto's own registry-trust checks (owned by SPEC-DX-CORRECTNESS-PARITY).
